title: NEOG Q3 Earnings & Revenues Top, Gross Margin Down, Stock Crashes
content:
Neogen Corporation NEOG reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of 9 cents, down 10% year over year.  However, the metric topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 125%.

Neogen’s Q3 Revenues

Revenues in the quarter decreased 4.4% on a year-over-year basis to $211.2 million. Meanwhile, core revenues increased 0.1%. Divestitures and discontinued product lines had a negative impact of 7.5%, while foreign currency had a positive impact of 3%. The metric topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.3%.

Following the announcement yesterday, NEOG stock fell 2.95% to close the session at $10.04.

Neogen’s Segments in Detail

The company's Food Safety segment registered revenues of $156.7 million in the fiscal third quarter, up 2.6% year over year. This consisted of 4% core revenue growth, a negative 5.4% impact of divestitures and discontinued product lines and a positive foreign currency impact of 4%. Our model projected Food Safety revenues to be $146.6 million for the fiscal third quarter.

Neogen Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseNeogen Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Neogen Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Neogen Corporation Quote

Revenues from the Animal Safety segment totaled $54.5 million, down 20.1% year over year. This consisted of an 8.7% core revenue decrease, a favorable 0.5% foreign currency impact and a negative 11.9% impact of divestitures and discontinued product lines. Our model’s projection for the business was $57.1 million.

Neogen’s Margin Details

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, gross profit declined 10.2% year over year to $99 million. The cost of revenues edged up 1.4% to $112.2 million. The gross margin contracted 303 basis points (bps) year over year to 46.9%.

Sales and marketing expenses amounted to $38.2 million, down 14.4% year over year, whereas administrative expenses increased 8.1% from the prior-year quarter’s level to $60 million. R&D expenses totaled $3.8 million, down 15.6% year over year. The quarter recorded an operating loss of $3.3 million compared to an operating profit of $5.4 million in the year-ago period.

Neogen’s Q3 Cash Position

Neogen’s cash and cash equivalents at the end of the fiscal third quarter totaled $137.1 million compared with $145.3 million at the end of the second quarter.

Cumulative net cash provided by operating activities came in at $53 million compared with $41.8 million a year ago.

Neogen’s Fiscal 2026 Outlook

The company raised its fiscal 2026 revenue projection, now expecting between $857 million and $860 million (previously $845 million-$855 million). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the same currently stands at $850.1 million.

Story Continues

Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be roughly $175 million (same as earlier).

Our Take on NEOG

Neogen ended the fiscal third quarter with better-than-expected earnings and revenues. However, both metrics were down on a year-over-year basis. The Animal Safety business experienced several third-party, supply-based setbacks, resulting in lower-than-anticipated growth. The contraction of gross margin in the quarter is also discouraging.

On a promising note, the Food Safety segment delivered another quarter of core revenue growth and was consistent with current market dynamics. Neogen made significant progress on its strategic initiatives, such as commercial prowess, high-impact innovation and operational efficiency, to stabilize and strengthen its core business. The raised revenue guidance for the year appears promising.

The company recently announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its global Genomics business to Zoetis Inc. for a purchase price of $160.0 million, subject to customary closing adjustments. The deal is expected to close by the end of the second quarter of fiscal year 2027.

NEOG’s Zacks Rank and Key Picks

Neogen currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks from the broader medical space are Globus Medical GMED, Phibro Animal Health PAHC and IDEXX Laboratories IDXX.

Globus Medical, currently sporting a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), reported fourth-quarter 2025 adjusted EPS of $1.28, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 20.76%. Revenues of $826.4 million beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.9%. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

GMED’s earnings yield of 4.8% favorably compares with the industry’s negative 1.6% yield. The company surpassed earnings estimates in three of the trailing four quarters and missed on one occasion, the average surprise being 18.8%.

Phibro Animal Health, carrying a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present, posted second-quarter fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of 87 cents, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 27.01%. Revenues of $373.9 million surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.72%.

PAHC has an estimated long-term earnings growth rate of 21.5% compared with the industry’s 12% growth. The company’s earnings outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 20.15%.

IDEXX Laboratories, carrying a Zacks Rank #2, reported a fourth-quarter 2025 EPS of $3.08, which surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 18%. Revenues of $1.09 billion topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.86%.

IDXX has an earnings yield of 2.5% compared with the industry’s negative 1.6% yield. The company’s earnings surpassed estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 6.11%.

title: Neogen Corporation Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Neogen Corporation Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Execution and Performance Drivers

Food Safety segment achieved 4% core growth, reaching market-level performance through improved commercial rigor and demand for indicator testing and culture media. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 22.8% due to disciplined cost control and a 9% sequential reduction in adjusted operating expenses. Animal Safety revenue declined 8.7% on a core basis, primarily driven by third-party supplier transitions, raw material shortages, and documentation issues rather than underlying demand weakness. Management is transitioning the commercial model from siloed regional operations to a unified, solutions-based global selling framework to better leverage the full product portfolio. Operational efficiency efforts are focused on centralizing the supply chain and implementing AI-enabled logistics to reduce the current high reliance on manual processes and labor costs. The company is reallocating resources by shifting to distribution partners in lower-impact markets to fund growth in high-priority geographic and customer segments.

Fiscal 2027 Outlook and Strategic Initiatives

The Petrifilm manufacturing transition remains on schedule for November 2026, with 100% of production equipment validated and SKU validation currently underway. Management expects significant free cash flow improvement in fiscal 2027 as capital expenditures for Petrifilm facilities subside and duplicative manufacturing costs are eliminated. Guidance for Q4 assumes a transition from currency tailwinds to headwinds and a measured recovery timeline for Animal Safety supply chain challenges. Strategic R&D investment in a research-scale Petrifilm line is intended to accelerate entry into new markets such as pharmaceuticals and cosmetics by enabling custom SKU prototyping. The divestiture of the genomics business, expected to close in Q2 fiscal 2027, is positioned to reduce net debt to adjusted EBITDA below 3x by the end of calendar 2026.

Risk Factors and Operational Adjustments

Global logistics disruptions, particularly near the Suez Canal, are driving high single-digit to low double-digit increases in freight and transportation costs. A quality issue at a third-party supplier for sample collection products led to higher scrap rates and negative gross margins for that category this quarter. Approximately 56% of operating expenses are currently tied to salaries and benefits, which management attributes to historical underinvestment in automation. Animal Safety headwinds include a global vitamin A shortage and production transitions by key partners in instruments and sodium bicarb.

Story Continues

Q&A Session Highlights

Resolution timeline for Animal Safety supplier disruptions

Management clarified that Q3 issues were supply-side only, involving three specific partners transitioning manufacturing sites or facing raw material shortages. The Q4 guidance remains 'meaningfully measured' as these external issues are not expected to be fully resolved within the next quarter.

Sustainability of 4% core growth in Food Safety

Management expressed confidence in sustaining growth by optimizing the portfolio toward higher-margin products and realigning sales resources. Customer sentiment is improving as food producers report volumes moving from 'declining' to 'flat,' though macro pressures like energy costs remain a factor.

Margin expansion opportunities beyond fiscal 2026

Future margin gains are expected from in-sourcing Petrifilm, resolving sample collection quality issues, and improving purchase price variance through better supplier management. A shift from legacy raw materials to finished goods is expected to lead to a 'meaningful decline' in inventory levels by fiscal 2027, further aiding margins.

title: Neogen (NEOG) Q3 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Wednesday, April 9, 2025 at 8 a.m. ET

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Chief Executive Officer — John AdentChief Financial Officer — David Naemura

TAKEAWAYS

Total Revenue -- $221 million reported, with foreign currency a negative 310 basis point impact compared to the prior year.Core Revenue Growth -- 0.2% growth, with "headwinds in genomics and sample collection" contributing over 400 basis points of drag to consolidated core revenue growth.Food Safety Segment Revenue -- $153 million, a decrease of 3.2% with core revenue growth of 1.5% offset by foreign currency.Food Safety Core Revenue (Ex-Sample Collection) -- 7% growth, driven by biosecurity, pathogen detection, food quality, and Petrifilm products.Animal Safety Segment Revenue -- $68 million, with a core revenue decline of 2.6%; core business outside genomics declined just over 1%.Global Genomics Core Revenue -- Down mid-single digits; differentiated bovine segment achieved low single-digit growth.Gross Margin -- 49.9%, representing a 120 basis point decrease from 51.1% last year; excluding special items, margin was down 30 basis points due to lower revenues.Adjusted EBITDA -- $49 million, or a 22% margin, flat sequentially and declining year over year on lower revenue.Adjusted Net Income and EPS -- $21 million and $0.10, respectively, compared to $26 million and $0.12 a year ago, mainly due to lower EBITDA and a higher tax rate.Free Cash Flow -- Outflow of approximately $14 million, improving by $49 million compared to Q3 2024.Refinancing Activity -- Term Loan A refinanced, extending maturity by 2.5 years and achieving a 60 basis point interest rate reduction.Full-Year Guidance Update -- Revenue outlook revised to approximately $895 million, adjusted EBITDA to $195 million, and free cash flow now projected as a $20 million outflow.Tariff Exposure -- CFO David Naemura stated: "If you just took kind of the last 12 months run rate and straight up applying tariffs ... you'd probably be around $30 million, close to it, $29 million. And of that, two-thirds of it roughly would be China ... this is predominantly Animal Safety."Leadership Changes -- A new Head of R&D, a new North America Commercial Organization head, a new commercial Head for North American Food Safety, and a new Chief Human Resources Officer were appointed; Chief Commercial Officer search to conclude in Q1 2026.Petrifilm Integration -- First two production lines installed; initial test production remains on track for fall 2025, with a phased SKU-by-SKU ramp-up model described as "a more gradual transition."Cost Actions -- Portfolio changes in late-stage consideration with net proceeds intended for debt reduction; further cost alignment actions underway targeting Q4 and fiscal 2026 impact.Regional Performance -- Latin America achieved double-digit core revenue growth; Asia Pacific grew mid-single digits; Europe and U.S./Canada decreased mid-single digits, with declines concentrated in genomics, sample collection, and associated categories.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email pr@fool.com

RISKS

CFO David Naemura said, "the macroeconomic uncertainty has led to somewhat of a pause taken by many customers and channel partners," contributing to a revenue shortfall of approximately $6 million in the quarter.John Adent noted, "the Food Safety market soften a bit at the end of the quarter," leading to underperformance relative to internal expectations and impacting full-year guidance.Core gross margin decreased by 120 basis points year over year; excluding integration and restructuring costs as well as the reclassification of certain expenses in the prior year period, Q3 gross margin was down 30 basis points year over year, primarily due to lower revenues.Free cash flow for the year guided to a $20 million outflow, with integration CapEx expected to remain elevated before tapering in subsequent fiscal years.

SUMMARY

The Neogen(NASDAQ:NEOG) call announced CEO John Adent's resignation, concurrent with material leadership transitions including new appointments across R&D, commercial, and HR positions. The company's integration of the Petrifilm product line continues, with initial test production planned for fall 2025 and a phased transition strategy expected to generate duplicate costs during the ramp-up. Management highlighted that macroeconomic softness, customer inventory caution, and global tariff volatility drove approximately $6 million of quarterly revenue underperformance and led to a reduction in full-year financial guidance. Strategic portfolio actions are entering advanced phases, with explanations that proceeds will be used for deleveraging, while free cash flow is pressured by ongoing capital expenditures and margin compression. The outlook for fiscal 2026 includes further cost realignment as the company responds to lower-than-anticipated revenue levels and heightened macroeconomic risk.

Food Safety segment core revenue excluding sample collection rose 7%, yet "disappointed" management due to falling short of double-digit growth expectations amid muted distributor stocking.Global Genomics weakness persisted, particularly outside bovine, offsetting stability in core Animal Safety and prompting further focus on bovine as "that's really the business that our restructuring is aimed at focusing around."Guidance and commentary suggest the bulk of the revenue miss stemmed from macro-driven distributor hesitancy and China softness, rather than execution missteps or integration delays.Recent completion of term loan refinancing and launch of portfolio actions demonstrated continued prioritization of debt reduction and balance sheet flexibility in a "very dynamic" trade and policy environment.Management signaled that Petrifilm integration costs will be dimensionalized and disclosed as SKU transfer progresses, indicating temporary cost overlap for fiscal 2026 as new capacity comes online.

INDUSTRY GLOSSARY

Petrifilm: Proprietary ready-to-use microbiological testing products developed as part of the acquired 3M Food Safety business for quantifying microorganisms in food and environment samples.Bovine Genomics: Genetic testing and analysis services focused on cattle, enabling trait selection, disease resistance, and productivity improvements for livestock producers.

Full Conference Call Transcript

John Adent: Thanks, Bill. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the earnings call for the third quarter of our 2025 fiscal year. You may have seen the press release issued earlier today announcing that I will be stepping down as CEO. It's been an honor to lead Neogen and I'm incredibly proud of the team we've built and everything we've accomplished, including making a significant amount of progress on the complex integration of a transformational acquisition. I would like to extend my sincere gratitude to the team for all their hard work and sacrifice over the last several years and firmly believe these efforts have put the company in a stronger position.

I will remain in my role while the Board conducts a search for my successor, and I'm fully committed to ensuring a smooth transition for our customers and employees. With that behind us, let's move into some color on the quarter. Over the course of the third quarter, we saw the broad development of uncertainty, primarily related to the goals and policies of the U.S. government, most notably deregulation, government spending cuts, tariffs and global trade. As we've all seen, the administration is aiming to reduce federal spending that has made cuts across a number of government agencies, including those relevant to food safety like the FDA and the USDA.

While these cuts could possibly affect the speed with which outbreaks of food-borne illness can be addressed or possibly delay or eliminate certain research spending, we don't currently see them as having a significant effect on food safety testing.
